notes: All amounts are in USD and are shown in full units (not millions). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
EBIT is proxied by the company’s “Operating earnings” (operating income equivalent). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

D&A is proxied by cash-flow “Depreciation and amortization” (separately from non-cash lease expense). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

Net working capital (NWC) uses the company-reported “Working capital” balance (current assets minus current liabilities) rather than a custom operating-NWC definition; this may differ from a strict DCF operating NWC build. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

NOL utilization percent is left null because the filing discloses gross loss carryforwards and valuation allowance but does not provide an explicit utilization rate suitable for a DCF utilization parameter. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
WACC is taken as a model input reference from StockAnalysis statistics (used as-is in the assumptions). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gww/statistics/))
Current_price reflects the latest available trade captured by the finance tool on 2026-03-20 (used for as_of_date 2026-03-21).

catalysts: Sustained underlying demand and improved mix within Endless Assortment/MonotaRO supporting mid-single-digit revenue growth.
Further margin normalization as exit/restructuring headwinds abate and cost structure benefits show through.
Conversion of supply-chain and technology investments into better availability/fill rates while maintaining working-capital discipline.
company_overview: W.W. Grainger is a broad-line distributor of maintenance, repair and operating (MRO) products and services, with operations primarily in North America and Japan (and it exited the U.K. market in Q4 2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

Financial reporting is organized around two operating segments: High-Touch Solutions N.A. and Endless Assortment (Japan / MonotaRO). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

FY2025 fundamentals: net sales of $17,942, operating earnings of $2,495, and depreciation & amortization of $254 (USD, in millions). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 net sales were $17,942 million (+4.5% YoY) with operating earnings of $2,495 million; effective tax rate was 25.6%. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
FY2025 capex was $684 million; the company guided FY2026 capex in a $550 to $650 million range. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
Grainger completed its U.K. market exit in Q4 2025 (Cromwell sale and Zoro U.K. business closure). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case assumes sales growth reverts to mid-single digits with operating margin gradually normalizing from the 2024–2025 restructuring/exit effects. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity is modeled as a gradual normalization from the elevated 2025 run-rate toward a ~3% of sales capex profile. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

Working-capital intensity is kept stable (modeled NWC at ~0.194–0.196 of sales) to avoid overstating free cash flow resilience. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

Terminal value uses an exit EV/EBITDA multiple broadly consistent with large listed industrial distributors’ observed valuation range. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/fast/statistics/))
key_risks: A macro-driven slowdown in industrial maintenance demand could pressure both volumes and gross profit dollars.

Working-capital volatility (inventory/receivables) may reduce free cash flow versus modeled NWC intensity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))
Execution risk related to U.K. exit and ongoing cost actions could introduce margin and tax-benefit uncertainty.

presentation.subtitle: DCF Base-Case & Multiples—W.W. Grainger (GWW)
valuation_summary: The DCF base-case applies a WACC of ~9.81% and a 2.0% terminal growth rate to reflect long-run reinvestment and macro risk. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gww/statistics/))

Forecast operating returns converge to a target EBIT margin of ~15.0% by 2030 (recovering from 2025’s ~13.9% operating margin). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000011/gww-20251231.htm))

The terminal exit multiple (16.0x EV/EBITDA) is set to be economically consistent with the distributor comp set rather than using an aggressive growth-premium multiple. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/fast/statistics/))
